common_name: Nippon Maiden Grass (Narrow-Leaf Chinese Silver Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist to well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Nippon is valued for its narrow, deep rosy-violet stems and compact, upright habit — more restrained and self-supporting than larger arching maiden grass cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist to well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Nippon is a compact, narrowly upright Miscanthus sinensis selection distinguished by deep rosy-violet coloring at the base of its slender, finely textured leaf blades, which arch gracefully without flopping. From late summer into fall, feathery, whisk-like pink-to-red flower panicles rise just above the foliage and gradually fade to beige as seed matures, providing extended fall and winter interest. Because Nippon holds a tighter, more upright clump than many maiden grass cultivars, it is well suited to smaller gardens, narrow borders, and situations where a self-supporting vertical accent is needed without staking. Note: Miscanthus sinensis can be invasive in some eastern states — check local invasive species guidance before planting near natural areas. Cut the clump back to 4-6 inches in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Rigoletto Maiden Grass (Compact White-Striped Silver Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist to well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Rigoletto is a Kurt Bluemel introduction that offers the crisp white-striped variegation of 'Variegatus' on a more compact, better-behaved clump.

directions: Plant in moist to well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Rigoletto is a densely-tufted Miscanthus sinensis cultivar bred by noted grass breeder Kurt Bluemel, offering narrow (about 1/2-inch wide), linear, arching green leaves boldly striped with gleaming white variegation. Rigoletto forms a tidier, more restrained clump (roughly 4-5 feet tall and 3-4 feet wide) than the larger, more open 'Variegatus', making it a better choice for smaller borders and mixed perennial plantings where a bright, textural accent is wanted without excessive bulk. In late summer into fall, feathery pink-to-red flower panicles rise above the variegated foliage and mature to beige. Note: Miscanthus sinensis can be invasive in some eastern states — check local invasive species guidance before planting near natural areas. Cut back to 4-6 inches in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Gnome Maiden Grass (Compact Fine-Textured Silver Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist to well-drained soil in full sun; Gnome is a compact Knoll Gardens selection with fine-textured foliage and early, softly colored flower plumes, well suited to smaller gardens.

directions: Plant in moist to well-drained soil in full sun; Gnome is a compact Miscanthus sinensis selection introduced by the UK's Knoll Gardens, forming dense, rounded mounds of fine, narrow green foliage that stay tidier and less sprawling than many larger maiden grass cultivars. Gnome typically reaches about 4-5 feet tall in bloom, with soft pink flower plumes appearing earlier in the season than many Miscanthus cultivars and gradually fading to a warm beige-gold as they mature. Its refined, fine-textured foliage and manageable size make Gnome a good choice for smaller gardens, mixed borders, and container culture. Note: Miscanthus sinensis can be invasive in some eastern states — check local invasive species guidance before planting near natural areas. Cut the clump back to 4-6 inches in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Lumen Gold Fountain Grass (Golden Dwarf Fountain Grass)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Lumen Gold is grown primarily for its glowing golden spring and early-summer foliage rather than for flower — a distinct departure from typical green-leaved fountain grass cultivars.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Lumen Gold (patented as PP27,435, also sold as 'JS Jommenik') is a compact, mounding Pennisetum alopecuroides selection grown chiefly for its striking golden-yellow foliage, which emerges bright gold in early spring, holds a glowing lemon-yellow color through early summer, and gradually matures to light green as the season progresses. The tight, dense mound habit reaches only 12-24 inches tall and 24-36 inches wide, making it considerably more compact than green-leaved fountain grass cultivars like Hameln, and well suited to container culture, rock gardens, and the front of sunny borders. Full sun is essential for the best gold coloration; in shade the foliage tends toward green and the habit loosens. Cut back to 4-6 inches in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Praline Fountain Grass (Sterile Dwarf Fountain Grass)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Praline is a sterile University of Georgia introduction bred not to self-seed, making it a well-behaved alternative to seed-producing fountain grass cultivars.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Praline (patented as PP 30,724, trial name 'Tift-H18') is a compact, sterile Pennisetum alopecuroides cultivar bred at the University of Georgia's ornamental grass breeding program specifically to eliminate the unwanted self-seeding of the species and many older cultivars. The tidy, rounded clump reaches roughly 18-30 inches tall and 30-42 inches wide, producing soft, fuzzy bottlebrush flower plumes in tan flushed with pink from midsummer into fall, fading to a warm wheat color that persists attractively through winter. Because Praline does not set viable seed, it is an excellent choice for gardeners in regions where Pennisetum alopecuroides has become weedy. Full sun and well-drained soil produce the densest, most floriferous clumps. Cut back to 4-6 inches in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Red Buttons Fountain Grass (Thunberg's Fountain Grass)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Red Buttons is less cold-hardy than Pennisetum alopecuroides cultivars and is best reserved for zone 7 and warmer, or grown as a striking summer annual farther north.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Red Buttons is a graceful, deciduous Pennisetum thunbergii cultivar forming an upright, arching clump of narrow, finely textured grassy leaves. In late summer, elongated, rosy-red feathery flower plumes rise well above the foliage on long, wiry stems, gradually fading to a soft buff-tan as they mature into fall, giving the plant an airy, two-toned effect especially effective backlit by low sun. Reaching about 2-3 feet tall and wide, Red Buttons is more compact and refined in texture than many Pennisetum alopecuroides selections. It is noticeably less cold-hardy than cultivars like Hameln or Karley Rose and is reliably perennial only from about zone 7 south; in colder zones it can be grown as a dramatic warm-season annual. Cut back to 4-6 inches in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Blue Tower Switchgrass (Giant Columnar Blue Switchgrass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained to moist, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Blue Tower is among the tallest upright switchgrass cultivars available and holds a strict columnar form without staking even at its full height.

directions: Plant in well-drained to moist, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Blue Tower is a dramatic, large-scale Panicum virgatum selection prized for its strictly columnar, non-flopping habit and striking blue-green summer foliage. Flowering stems can reach up to 8 feet tall, making Blue Tower one of the tallest switchgrass cultivars in general cultivation — a bold vertical accent and effective seasonal screen or backdrop planting. The blue-green foliage transitions to warm golden tones in fall and winter, and airy, fine-textured flower panicles appear from late summer into fall. Like the species, Blue Tower is a North American prairie native that is exceptionally adaptable, tolerating heat, drought once established, clay soils, and occasional flooding, remaining reliably self-supporting in exposed, windy sites. Cut the clump back to 4-6 inches in late winter before new growth emerges.
